source.title_or_context: AF = atrial fibrillation; AVB = atrioventricular block; AVJ = atrioventricular junction; BBB = bundle branch block; b.p.m. = beats per minute; CIED = cardiovascular implantable electronic device; CRT = cardiac resynchronization therapy; CRT-D = defibrillator with cardiac resynchronization therapy; CSM = carotid sinus massage; DDD = dual-chamber, atrioventricular pacing; ECG = electrocardiogram; EPS = electrophysiology study; HF = heart failure; HFrEF = heart failure with reduced ejection fraction; HV = His–ventricular interval; ICD = implantable cardioverter-defibrillator; ILR = implantable loop recorder; LBBB = left bundle branch block; LV = left ventricle; LVEF = left ventricular ejection fraction; MI = myocardial infarction; MRI = magnetic resonance imaging; NYHA = New York Heart Association; OMT = optimal medical therapy; RBBB = right bundle branch block; RV = right ventricular; SAS = sleep apnoea syndrome; SND = sinus node dysfunction; SR = sinus rhythm; TAVI = transcatheter aortic valve implantation. aClass of recommendation. bLevel of evidence. cCSM should not be undertaken in patients with previous transient ischaemic attack, stroke, or known carotid stenosis. Carotid auscultation should be performed before CSM. If a carotid bruit is present, carotid ultrasound should be performed to exclude carotid disease. dComplete blood counts, prothrombin time, partial thromboplastin time, serum creatinine, and electrolytes. eIn asymptomatic narrow QRS complex and 2:1 AVB, pacing may be avoided if supra-Hisian block is clinically suspected (concomitant Wenckebach is observed and block disappears with exercise) or demonstrated at EPS. fWhenever pacing is indicated in neuromuscular disease, CRT or an implantable cardioverter-defibrillator should be considered according to relevant guidelines. gCombination of MRI conditional generator and lead(s) from the same manufacturer.

table_assessment.assessment_notes: The isolated summary table contains 16 assertion-bearing rows on pacing, device management, MRI, follow-up, and patient-centred care. It also contains medication-directed antibiotic prophylaxis and heparin-bridging rows, so modality/content is mixed. The final patient-centred recommendation repeats an independently materialized recommendation unit, so duplicate adjudication is required before evaluation use.

entities.surface_form: High-degree or complete AVB after cardiac surgery
complete AVB with low or no escape rhythm

header_path: Recommendations for cardiac pacing after cardiac surgery and heart transplantation

normative_assertions.notes: At least five days of observation is indicated to assess persistence after cardiac surgery.
A shorter observation period is permitted when resolution is unlikely because escape rhythm is low or absent.

text_units.verbatim_text: High-degree or complete AVB after cardiac surgery: a period of clinical observation of at least 5 days is indicated to assess whether the rhythm disturbance is transient and resolves. However, this observation period can be shortened in the case of complete AVB with low or no escape rhythm when resolution is unlikely.

entities.surface_form: Patients requiring pacing after mechanical tricuspid valve replacement
implantation of a transvalvular RV lead

header_path: Recommendations for cardiac pacing after cardiac surgery and heart transplantation

normative_assertions.notes: Transvalvular RV-lead implantation should be avoided after mechanical tricuspid valve replacement.

text_units.verbatim_text: Patients requiring pacing after mechanical tricuspid valve replacement: implantation of a transvalvular RV lead should be avoided.

entities.surface_form: patients with complete or high-degree AVB that persists for 24 - 48 h after TAVI

header_path: Recommendations for cardiac pacing after TAVI

normative_assertions.notes: Permanent pacing is recommended for AV block persisting 24–48 hours after TAVI.

text_units.verbatim_text: Permanent pacing is recommended in patients with complete or high-degree AVB that persists for 24 - 48 h after TAVI.

entities.surface_form: patients with new-onset alternating BBB after TAVI

header_path: Recommendations for cardiac pacing after TAVI

normative_assertions.notes: Permanent pacing is recommended for new-onset alternating BBB after TAVI.

text_units.verbatim_text: Permanent pacing is recommended in patients with new-onset alternating BBB after TAVI.

entities.surface_form: patients with RBBB and no indication for permanent pacing

header_path: Recommendations for cardiac pacing after TAVI

normative_assertions.notes: Prophylactic pacemaker implantation is recommended against before TAVI when RBBB is present without a pacing indication.

text_units.verbatim_text: Prophylactic permanent pacemaker implantation is not indicated before TAVI in patients with RBBB and no indication for permanent pacing.

entities.surface_form: patients with congenital complete or high-degree AVB
Symptoms ii. Pauses >3× the cycle length of the ventricular escape rhythm iii. Broad QRS escape rhythm iv. Prolonged QT interval v. Complex ventricular ectopy vi. Mean daytime heart rate <50 b.p.m.

header_path: Recommendations for cardiac pacing in patients with congenital heart disease

normative_assertions.notes: Pacing is conditional on at least one of six explicitly listed risk factors.
source_trigger_texts: is recommended if one of the following risk factors is present

text_units.verbatim_text: In patients with congenital complete or high-degree AVB, pacing is recommended if one of the following risk factors is present: i. Symptoms ii. Pauses >3× the cycle length of the ventricular escape rhythm iii. Broad QRS escape rhythm iv. Prolonged QT interval v. Complex ventricular ectopy vi. Mean daytime heart rate <50 b.p.m.

entities.surface_form: patients with neuromuscular diseases such as myotonic dystrophy type 1 and any second- or third-degree AVB or HV ≥70 ms, with or without symptoms

header_path: Recommendations for cardiac pacing in rare diseases

normative_assertions.notes: Permanent pacing is indicated for the stated neuromuscular disease and conduction findings regardless of symptoms.

text_units.verbatim_text: In patients with neuromuscular diseases such as myotonic dystrophy type 1 and any second- or third-degree AVB or HV ≥70 ms, with or without symptoms, permanent pacing is indicated. f

header_path: Recommendations regarding device implantations and peri-operative management

normative_assertions.notes: Pre-operative antibiotic prophylaxis is recommended within one hour before skin incision to reduce CIED infection risk.

text_units.verbatim_text: Administration of pre-operative antibiotic prophylaxis within 1 h of skin incision is recommended to reduce the risk of CIED infection.

header_path: Recommendations regarding device implantations and peri-operative management

normative_assertions.notes: Heparin bridging is recommended against in anticoagulated patients.

text_units.verbatim_text: Heparin bridging of anticoagulated patients is not recommended.

entities.surface_form: until the patient has been afebrile for at least 24 h

header_path: Recommendations regarding device implantations and peri-operative management

normative_assertions.notes: Permanent implantation is recommended against while the patient has fever.
Implantation should be scheduled only after at least 24 hours afebrile.

text_units.verbatim_text: Permanent pacemaker implantation is not recommended in patients with fever. Pacemaker implantation should be delayed until the patient has been afebrile for at least 24 h.

header_path: Recommendations for performing magnetic resonance imaging in pacemaker patients

normative_assertions.notes: MRI is explicitly permitted for MRI-conditional pacemaker systems when manufacturer instructions are followed.

text_units.verbatim_text: In patients with MRI-conditional pacemaker systems, g MRI can be performed safely following the manufacturer's instructions.

entities.surface_form: haemodynamic-compromising bradyarrhythmia refractory to intravenous chronotropic drugs

normative_assertions.notes: Temporary transvenous pacing is recommended for haemodynamically compromising bradyarrhythmia refractory to IV chronotropic drugs.

text_units.verbatim_text: Temporary transvenous pacing is recommended in cases of haemodynamic-compromising bradyarrhythmia refractory to intravenous chronotropic drugs.

header_path: Recommendation when pacing is no longer indicated

normative_assertions.notes: Management when pacing is no longer indicated should use individualized risk–benefit and shared decision-making with the patient.

text_units.verbatim_text: When pacing is no longer indicated, the decision on management strategy should be based on an individual risk–benefit analysis in a shared decision-making process together with the patient.

entities.surface_form: patients with pacemakers who have difficulties in attending in-office visits

header_path: Recommendations for pacemaker and cardiac resynchronization therapy-pacemaker follow-up

normative_assertions.notes: Remote management is recommended to reduce in-office visits for patients who have difficulty attending them.

text_units.verbatim_text: Remote device management is recommended to reduce the number of in-office follow-up visits in patients with pacemakers who have difficulties in attending in-office visits (e.g. due to reduced mobility or other commitments, or according to patient preference).

entities.surface_form: device component that has been recalled or is on advisory

header_path: Recommendations for pacemaker and cardiac resynchronization therapy-pacemaker follow-up

normative_assertions.notes: Remote monitoring is recommended for recalled/advisory components to detect actionable events early, particularly in high-risk patients.

text_units.verbatim_text: Remote monitoring is recommended in the case of a device component that has been recalled or is on advisory, to enable early detection of actionable events in patients, particularly those who are at increased risk (e.g. in case of pacemaker dependency).

entities.surface_form: patients considered for a pacemaker or CRT
principles of patient-centred care and shared decision-making

header_path: Recommendation regarding patient-centred care in cardiac pacing and cardiac resynchronization therapy

normative_assertions.notes: The pacing decision should be evidence-based and individualized.
source_trigger_texts: the decision should be based on

normative_assertions.notes: Integrated care and patient-centred shared decision-making are explicitly recommended.

text_units.verbatim_text: In patients considered for a pacemaker or CRT, the decision should be based on the best available evidence with consideration of individual risk–benefits of each option, the patient's preferences, and goals of care, and it is recommended to follow an integrated care approach and use the principles of patient-centred care and shared decision-making in the consultation.
